Action Plan:
1. Start ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily after food for left elbow swelling (presumed bursitis); discontinue if heartburn occurs.
2. Arrange blood tests for inflammatory markers, infection, rheumatological antibodies, and gout screening; blood test forms to be sent to patient, with instructions included.
3. Arrange follow-up review (in-person, video, or phone as preferred by patient) after blood results are available, or sooner if symptoms worsen.
4. Advise patient to seek urgent assessment if elbow becomes very red, very painful, or if redness spreads/intensifies (to rule out septic arthritis/emergency).
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Swelling and mild warmth over left elbow noted approximately 1 week ago; not painful; no preceding trauma or injury; patient feels well otherwise.
- No impairment in movement or significant tenderness. Mild discomfort only adjacent to swelling.
- No prior episodes of similar swelling.
- Job non-physical (desk job).
- Past medical history: Osteoarthritis (previously diagnosed by GP a few years ago); no history of eczema or other systemic disease noted.
- Allergies: Peanuts.
- No known drug allergies.
- Medications: None currently.
- Social history: Runs 2–3 times a week; reports being mobile, active, and healthy.

Objective:
- Video assessment of left elbow: Visible swelling; mildly warm compared to surrounding skin.
- No marked tenderness on tip of elbow; slight abnormal sensation adjacent to swelling.
- Elbow movement preserved and normal.
- Overlying skin: Slightly dry on tip of elbow.
- No clinical signs of systemic infection, no marked erythema or acute features of septic arthritis on inspection.
- No other physical findings documented.
- No vitals or lab results available.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Left elbow swelling (presumed bursitis):
   - Assessment: Likely olecranon bursitis (non-infective), based on swelling, localized warmth, no pain or significant trauma history.
   - Differential diagnosis: Gout, early septic arthritis, inflammatory arthritis (including possible exacerbation of osteoarthritis).
   - Investigations planned: Blood tests for inflammatory markers, infection, rheumatological antibodies (including autoimmune screen), and gout screening.
   - Treatment planned: Ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily after food; monitor for gastrointestinal side effects; discontinue if heartburn occurs.
   - Relevant referrals: None at this time; follow-up arranged for review.

2. Osteoarthritis (background):
   - Assessment: Past diagnosis; no acute exacerbation recorded at this visit.
   - Differential diagnosis: N/A.
   - Investigations planned: None directly; blood tests as above may provide additional information.
   - Treatment planned: Nil at this time beyond current management above.
   - Relevant referrals: None.

Quality checks:
● Clinically expected elements missing: No medication reconciliation beyond current statement; no documented blood pressure, temperature, systemic review, or specific infection screening in this consult.
● Internal conflicts: None identified.
● Transcript quality: Minor conversational repetitions present; generally clear, all relevant clinical content documented.
